name: Pool Corporation (POOLCORP)

corporate_actions.event: CEO transition: John Watwood succeeded Peter Arvan; $0.21/share one-time CEO transition costs in Q2 2026
Q3 2026: sales +4% (price 3%, volume 1%), op margin 11.4%; adj. EPS guide $10.87-11.17 reaffirmed; Investor Day planned H1 2027

geography.fx_notes: Predominantly US (Sun Belt: Florida, Texas, California, Arizona key markets) with small Europe and Australia operations; precise split not extracted this run (10-K geographic note). INFERENCE: US ~90%+.

company_fcf.definition: Net cash from operations (115% of NI); company does not headline FCF

lease.source_id: US GAAP filer; operating leases in opex

acquisitions.notes: 'Programmatic M&A' a stated priority; no material 2026 deal cited; historically small tuck-ins

management.senior_turnover_5y: CEO changed twice in ~5 years (Manuel Perez de la Mesa -> Peter Arvan 2021 -> John Watwood 2026)
management.succession_notes: External/new CEO with one-time transition costs
management.guidance_record: Weak 2023-2025: multiple EPS guidance cuts during housing/discretionary downturn (not re-verified individually); 2026 reaffirmed

ownership.controlling_holders: None; widely held (Berkshire Hathaway held a stake historically - not re-verified)

evidence: Maintenance-driven recurring revenue base (chemicals, replacement equipment) [S1]
Installed base of pools requires ongoing care
New construction/discretionary is the swing factor [S1]
A.rationale: Majority non-discretionary maintenance; discretionary build/renovation adds cyclicality.

evidence: Largest distributor; 'network of local sales centers backed by scale' [S1]
B.rationale: Density and scale moat in a niche.

evidence: Network consolidation lowers cost to serve [S1]
C.rationale: Scale advantages measurable but margins compressed post-COVID.

F.rationale: Turnover and misses through the downturn.

sector_specific.notes: Construction: new pool construction and irrigation/landscape (housing-linked) are cyclical components; company historically cites ~60%+ of sales as maintenance/repair (not re-verified). Acquisition contribution not disclosed for 2026 (small).

gates.notes: Leverage 1.8x; OCF>NI; no UK consumer exposure; US residential discretionary exposure is a portfolio-correlation consideration (not a G7 trigger as defined).

bull_points: Maintenance base and installed-base growth support resilient revenue (S1)
Network density and private label give scale advantages (S1)
Cyclical trough in new pool construction offers recovery leverage (S1)
bear_points: Three years of declining/flat revenue (2023-2025) and margin compression (S3)
New CEO with strategy reset; prior guidance cuts (S1)
thesis_breakers: Gross margin below 28.5% for a full year
